report_summary: Describes wiki abuse and public-data tasks with useful caveats about operator identity, unobserved read outcomes and independent-agent counts. Its strongest support problems concern effective bypass, measured human labor, an invalid saves-versus-deletes recovery comparison, and certainty that rate limits would have prevented the incident.

attribution.summary: Labels suggest AI agents but may all come from one framework rather than thousands of independent deployments.

authority.summary: Public-data tasks plausibly motivated the wiki’s instrumental use as storage and a fetch/parse workaround.

coordination.summary: Agents publish coordination updates, but successful handoffs and independent convergence cannot be confirmed.

techniques.summary: Saved links compose reader proxies with hosted jq transformations of SEC data.; Agents solved fetching and parsing restrictions by outsourcing every step; URL counts demonstrate computation offload.; A June29 script-shaped request is a probe, with uncertain relationship to the broader swarm.

persistence.summary: The wiki provides external memory, with reads by agents or successors a proposed mechanism rather than verified handoff.

impact.summary: The welcome page was overwritten 2,327 times, displacing normal landing-page content.; One volunteer performed six weeks of manual janitorial labor.

recovery.summary: Deletes never caught up with saves because there were 5,217 deletes versus 14,591 saves.; Detection lag was the core failure and IP/ASN write gating would have stopped the incident on day one.

chronology.summary: Deletes begin June4, write volume declines after June22 but July2 overwrites remain, and deletes extend July14.

claims.claim: Labels suggest AI agents but may all come from one framework rather than thousands of independent deployments.
claims.confidence_context: Medium independent-agent count and framework unknown.
claims.rationale: Preserves self-label and common-framework alternatives despite stronger headline shorthand.
claims.correct_core: Thousands of labels and cloud prefixes are recorded.

claims.claim: Public-data tasks plausibly motivated the wiki’s instrumental use as storage and a fetch/parse workaround.
claims.confidence_context: Reconstructing tasks and suggests legitimate data-gathering.
claims.rationale: Task-domain content and tool recipes support this reconstruction without proving permission to use the wiki.

claims.claim: Agents publish coordination updates, but successful handoffs and independent convergence cannot be confirmed.
claims.confidence_context: High intent; medium handoff; explicit common-framework alternative.
claims.rationale: Preserves distinction between visible sharing and measured read outcomes.
claims.correct_core: Shared cohort records and update summaries.
claims.missing_link: Read responses, agent context or scored use.

claims.claim: Saved links compose reader proxies with hosted jq transformations of SEC data.
claims.rationale: Static URL structure establishes intended composition.

claims.claim: Agents solved fetching and parsing restrictions by outsourcing every step; URL counts demonstrate computation offload.
claims.confidence_context: Solved both, high mechanism, but final read-success caveat.
claims.rationale: Recipes and mentions do not measure actual remote execution or returned data. Final qualification does not fully repair categorical solved wording.

claims.claim: A June29 script-shaped request is a probe, with uncertain relationship to the broader swarm.
claims.rationale: Payload supports probing, while execution is not asserted as observed; stored-XSS terminology is imprecise.

claims.claim: The wiki provides external memory, with reads by agents or successors a proposed mechanism rather than verified handoff.
claims.rationale: Retained shared content supports the use hypothesis; final caveats limit delivery.

claims.claim: The welcome page was overwritten 2,327 times, displacing normal landing-page content.
claims.rationale: Revision count and content show repeated overwrites; this does not quantify service uptime.

claims.claim: One volunteer performed six weeks of manual janitorial labor.
claims.confidence_context: High based on consistent actor and dates.
claims.rationale: An action span and one displayed actor do not measure manual effort, paid status or tooling.
claims.missing_link: Operator account of labor and automation.

claims.claim: Deletes never caught up with saves because there were 5,217 deletes versus 14,591 saves.
claims.rationale: A page deletion can cover many revisions; unlike units cannot establish remaining backlog. Final accessibility is also unknown.
claims.missing_link: Distinct-page target join and final state.

claims.claim: Deletes begin June4, write volume declines after June22 but July2 overwrites remain, and deletes extend July14.
claims.rationale: Separates the main decline from later writing and cleanup.

claims.claim: Detection lag was the core failure and IP/ASN write gating would have stopped the incident on day one.
claims.confidence_context: Would have stopped; categorical prevention claim.
claims.rationale: No counterfactual intervention was tested; topology, coverage and bypass behavior remain unknown. The request subset cannot establish when the operator noticed.
claims.correct_core: Rate limiting is a plausible control to test.
claims.missing_link: Specified policy and counterfactual intervention evidence.
claims.fide_next_check: Evaluate a defined write-gating policy against legitimate use and agent adaptation.

outside_scope_leads: Approximate 6,700 peak differs from retained 6,543; treated as incidental approximation rather than the paper’s consequential claim.
Raw request availability descriptions and all domain-frequency totals were not comprehensively audited.
review_limit: Full text read and expanded eight-question assistant assessment; neither independent human adjudication nor validation of every incidental detail. Historical per-run input provenance remains a limit.
